articles.title: Department of War Publishes Second Release of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Files on WAR.GOV/UFO
articles.summary: The Department of War says it is publishing the second release of declassified and historical Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena files as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, or PURSUE. The release states that the collection remains housed on WAR.GOV/UFO and that additional files will be released on a rolling basis. Assistant to the Secretary of War for Public Affairs and Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell is named as the source of the statement. The Department says WAR.GOV/UFO has received over 1 billion hits worldwide since its May 8, 2026 launch, which it frames as evidence of major public interest in the topic and in the Trump administration's transparency effort. The statement adds that the Department of War and agency partners are working on a third UAP file release, which will be announced in the near future.

articles.title: Dr. Phil accuses US government of lying ‘straight to our face’ for ignoring legitimate UFO reports
articles.summary: Phil accuses US government of lying ‘straight to our face’ for ignoring legitimate UFO reports See more of our coverage in your search results. Phil McGraw accused the Pentagon of lying “straight to our face” and ignoring the massive number of UFO sightings reported by the general public — despite civilians being responsible for seeing the majority of the activity. The famed TV host sensationally claimed Wednesday that there has been “a conscious, policy-driven decision to deceive the American people about what was going on in the skies” for decades — and that “we’re not getting the truth from our government. ” “[The government] has turned a blind eye to sightings by most Americans,” McGraw said in a video posted on his X account.

articles.title: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events
articles.summary: Exeter UFO Festival 2026: Your complete guide to out-of-this-world speakers and events - The Exeter UFO Festival is a Labor Day weekend tradition celebrating the 1965 "Incident at Exeter. " - Hosted by the Exeter-Area Kiwanis Club, the two-day event features UFO expert talks, a parade, and an alien costume contest. - Activities include trolley rides to the 1965 sighting location and continuous showings of historical videos. - Proceeds from the festival and a special police patch sale support local children's charities and scholarships. If you’ve walked through downtown Exeter lately, you may have spotted neon‑green alien faces peering from storefronts and posters — a sure sign that the UFO Festival is about to return.
